title: Phase-shifted tenant reset and cross-region drift reconciliation
creator: Arielle Park
description:
Problem: Reserved-capacity tenants across multi-region deployments are observing transient quota anomalies when their reset windows overlap with regional maintenance windows, tenant timezone offsets, or daylight-savings transitions. Symptoms include temporary double-counting of burst usage, incorrect remaining-balance displays in Console, and sporadic rate-limit violations despite backend state indicating limits were decremented. These issues are correlated with: (1) asynchronous reset anchors per region, (2) lease handoff races during rolling maintenance, and (3) delayed reconciliation of in-flight tokenized requests against the canonical usage ledger.

Goals: Provide a robust algorithm and migration plan to ensure deterministic per-tenant quota resets that: (a) align to tenant-configured anchors (UTC vs. tenant timezone), (b) tolerate rolling infra upgrades and region failovers, and (c) avoid short-window double-counts or undercounts for reserved and burst buckets. The solution should be backward compatible for hosted customers and require a migration path for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Proposal summary: Introduce a phase-shifted reset protocol plus a reconciliation window. Key pieces: (1) each tenant will have a canonical reset epoch recorded in the central ledger (epoch_anchor), which is the authoritative reset time used by all regions; (2) regional agents will perform a lightweight pre-reset lock and a short phase-shift window (default 2 minutes) where they move from pre-reset to active-reset states, agreeing with leader via lease; (3) during the phase-shift window we mark in-flight tokens with a reset-generation tag so downstream counters apply to either prior or new epoch deterministically; (4) reconciliation worker scans drifted counters for up to 24 hours and performs idempotent corrections, writing audit entries for every adjust; (5) provide a console-visible “expected reset window” per tenant and an opt-in migration mode that allows progressive rollout.

Design decisions and trade-offs: We avoid global synchronous resets (too brittle at scale). The phase-shifted approach trades slight delay for correctness and reduced cross-region contention. Reconciliation is eventual (within configured SLA) to keep request path fast; however, we will surface temporary UI caveats and a metrics tag to differentiate pre-reconciled balances. We keep reserved capacity quotas (monthly commits) treated as primary ledger entries; burst buckets are derived and recalculated during reconciliation to avoid double-bursting.

Compatibility and migration: For hosted customers, enable migration flag tenant.epoch_migration_state: "scheduled" -> "active". Default epoch_anchor set based on customer's billing preference (UTC start-of-day or tenant-local). For Dedicated/Private, provide a one-shot migration utility that writes epoch_anchor to the local control-plane DB and coordinates with on-prem agents via an agent handshake. CLI and Console flows documented in the migration guide.

Instrumentation and observability: New time-series metrics: quota.reset.leader_election.latency, quota.reset.phase_shift.duration, quota.reconcile.count, quota.reconcile.adjust_amount, and per-tenant quota.audit_events (sampled). Add trace spans for reset_leader.acquire, reset_phase_shift.start, reconcile.scan, reconcile.apply.

Rollout plan: 1) Implement central ledger epoch_anchor + API (backend only) behind feature flag; 2) Deploy regional agents with phase-shift capability in canary region for low-traffic tenants; 3) Run reconciliation workers in read-only mode to simulate adjustments for 48 hours and collect delta telemetry; 4) Enable active migration for 5% of hosted tenants and monitor errors for 72 hours; 5) Gradually increase to 100% and then backfill reconciliation for remaining historical drift. For Dedicated customers we provide scheduled maintenance windows with coordinated migration steps.

Testing and validation: Unit tests for tag propagation and idempotent adjust operations. Integration tests simulate cross-region reset overlaps, leader flaps, and network partitions. Chaos test: induce region clock skew and rolling restarts to validate no double-counting occurs. End-to-end acceptance: sample of tenants should show balanced token counts before and after migration with <0.1% net correction after reconciliation.

Security and compliance: Adjustments and audit events are stored in the audit log stream and linked to customer billing exports. Because reconciliation may create retroactive adjustments, we include tamper-evident checksums and require approvals for adjustments above threshold.

KPIs to monitor post-rollout: reduction in reported Console balance discrepancies, reconciliation adjust volume, number of rate-limit surprise incidents, and mean time to reconcile (target < 12 hours for 95th percentile).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Canonical epoch_anchor API exists and can be assigned per tenant.
2) Regional agents perform phase-shifted resets with leader lease and emit reset-generation tag on in-flight requests.
3) Reconciliation worker detects and corrects drift within 24 hours in testbed.
4) Console shows expected reset window and surfaces reconciliation-in-progress badge.
5) No increase in production request latency beyond 1% P95 attributable to reset flow.
6) Migration path documented and validated with one Dedicated customer pilot.
tasks: Add epoch_anchor field to tenant ledger and API
Implement reset leader election and pre-reset lock for regional agents
Tag in-flight requests with reset-generation and propagate through usage pipeline
Build reconciliation worker with idempotent adjust operations and audit logging
Console: show expected reset window and migration status
Instrumentation and dashboards for new metrics
